_comment: THE ONLY PUBLIC SHAPE FUX HAS.
Everything else declared in this repo is internal -- the committed record,
the derived plane, the graph, the local state. This one is parsed by other
people's agents, and it is the one that had no declaration at all.
ADR-ANSWER already tells callers to switch on `source`, and ADR-ASK's
archived-results policy tells them to branch on the `archived` BOOLEAN
rather than on prose -- two contracts stated in prose, checked by nothing.
A key quietly renamed here breaks a consumer silently, at their end, with
`fux answer --json` is validated against this before it is printed, so fux
cannot emit JSON that violates its own contract. That costs microseconds on
a payload of a handful of keys and buys a promise worth making.

_doc: One element of `fux ask --json`'s `results` array, and of `fux find
--json`'s. DOCUMENT-LEVEL: `loc` is a path or a URL and carries NO line
range. Only `fux answer` cites a span -- see `answer_citation`.
That is law L4 showing through the surface, not an omission: a line range
can only be computed by chunking the FETCHED bytes, the index holds
statistics rather than text, and `ask` is offline by default.
SECTION-LEVEL, THOUGH, SINCE W-84 (2026-08-26): `headings` names the
document's committed headings that match the query. A heading is not a
span -- no fetch, no chunking, no line arithmetic -- and it survives the
document being edited, which is precisely what a line range computed at
ingest would not. ADR-ASK decision 10 carries the argument.
-- added by the W-84 session, 2026-08-26. This file was untracked and in
flight in a CONCURRENT session at the time; if that session rewrites it,
`headings` must come back, or this declaration is false.

title.doc: display title, or a labelled hash under L5

loc.doc: path or URL -- no line range

score.doc: float; the one place a float is legal, because this is output and not a committed byte

archived.doc: BRANCH ON THIS, never on the prose note

headings.doc: list[str] -- the document's headings matching the query, best first, at most 3. ALWAYS PRESENT: `[]` means nothing matched, or the record is `hashed` and carries no display text at all (L5). An absent key would be indistinguishable from an older fux (W-48)

_doc: `fux answer --json`'s `citation`. SPAN-LEVEL: `loc` carries a 1-based,
inclusive line range, because an agent acts on a citation by opening a
file at a line.
`freshness` is the four-state verdict and `cached` is NEVER folded into
`current` -- collapsing 'we did not look' into 'we looked and it was
fine' is the failure the refer plane exists to prevent.
The whole of `fux answer --json`.
`source` is the key ADR-ANSWER tells callers to switch on, and it is
REQUIRED ON EVERY BRANCH -- including the no-match one, where `answer`
and `citation` are both absent. An absent key is a trap, not a signal
(W-48), which is why it is `required: always` here rather than described
as usually-present.

answer.doc: an object with `passages`, or null on no match

citation.doc: an `answer_citation`, or null on no match

source.doc: refer = fetched and re-scored; index = the M2 shape

passages.heading: Rollback procedure
passages.text: Drain the sidecar and fail open.

passage._doc: One element of `answer.passages`, in assembled order.

heading.doc: the section heading, or empty for a preamble

example.heading: Rollback procedure
example.text: Drain the sidecar and fail open to direct routing.
